title: The three things your backtest is quietly lying to you about
author: socialwhizca
selftext:
Every backtest I built looked amazing and it took me a while to learn why they don't survive contact with reality. Three culprits, in order of how much they burned me:

One, slippage and fills. The backtest assumes you got filled at the ideal price. Live, you don't, especially in fast moves. Two, spread. Most people model it as a flat constant when it's not, it widens exactly when your strategy is most active. Running live on AvaTrade the real intraday spread behaviour looked nothing like my flat assumption, and that alone explained a big chunk of the gap. Three, data quality, survivorship bias and missing gaps mean you backtested a market that never existed.

None of these are the model's fault, they're everything around the model. If your live results trail your backtest, I'd bet it's one of these three before it's your logic. Which of the three has bitten you hardest?

comments.body: Honestly? For me , it must be over fitting parameters/strats to find the most performant path. Walk forward can also be over fitted with enough permutations and experimentation. Its just easy to do with AI

comments.author: supferrets
comments.body: You can eliminate a lot of issues by drafting a trade specification and a frozen hypothesis, then running adversarial review on it and remediating the issues. You can take an even more rigorous approach by producing a development contract, assurance case, and a claim-argument-evidence matrix with the same review/adjudication/remediation process.
